subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised time are allocated for the final piece in the AQA GCSE Art and Design Externally Set Assignment?
questions.explain: AQA's Externally Set Assignment concludes with 10 hours of supervised time to produce the final response.

questions.q: What percentage of the total GCSE marks does Component 2 (Externally Set Assignment) contribute?
questions.explain: Component 2 is worth 40% of the GCSE, while Component 1 (Portfolio) is worth 60%.

questions.q: From which date are the AQA Externally Set Assignment question papers made available each year?
questions.explain: AQA releases the Externally Set Assignment papers on 1 January so preparatory work can begin.

questions.q: How does a student begin their response to the Externally Set Assignment?
options: They design their own starting point from scratch
They select one starting point from those set in the paper
They must respond to every starting point on the paper
They continue a project from Component 1
questions.explain: The paper offers several starting points and the student chooses one to develop a personal response.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the preparatory period before the supervised time?
options: To sit a written theory exam
To develop, refine and record ideas in response to the chosen starting point
To complete the final piece early
questions.explain: The preparatory period lets students research, experiment and plan before producing the final piece.

questions.q: Can a student bring their preparatory work into the supervised sessions?
options: No, preparatory work must be handed in before the supervised time
Yes, preparatory work may be referred to during the supervised time
Only written notes may be brought in
Only if the teacher photocopies it first
questions.explain: Students may use their preparatory work for reference while producing the supervised final piece.

questions.q: What must be produced entirely under supervised conditions?
options: The final outcome(s) that resolve the response
questions.explain: The 10-hour supervised time is used to produce the final piece that resolves the preparatory work.

questions.q: Which four assessment objectives must the Externally Set Assignment address?
questions.explain: AQA's four assessment objectives are Develop (AO1), Refine (AO2), Record (AO3) and Present (AO4).

questions.q: How are the assessment objectives weighted across the Externally Set Assignment?
options: All four assessment objectives carry equal marks
Only AO1 and AO4 are assessed
questions.explain: The four assessment objectives are weighted equally, each carrying 25% of the marks.

questions.q: Which assessment objective relates to recording ideas, observations and insights relevant to intentions?
questions.explain: AO3 requires students to record ideas, observations and insights relevant to their intentions as work progresses.

questions.q: Which assessment objective involves refining work by experimenting with media, materials, techniques and processes?
questions.explain: AO2 focuses on refining and experimenting with appropriate media, materials, techniques and processes.

questions.q: Which assessment objective requires developing ideas through investigations demonstrating critical understanding of sources?
questions.explain: AO1 requires developing ideas through investigations and showing critical understanding of sources.

questions.q: Which assessment objective is concerned with presenting a personal and meaningful response that realises intentions?
questions.explain: AO4 assesses the presentation of a personal, meaningful response that realises intentions.

questions.q: May the 10 hours of supervised time be split across more than one session?
options: No, it must be one continuous 10-hour session
Yes, it may be divided into more than one supervised session
Only into two sessions of exactly 5 hours
Only if the exam is done at home
questions.explain: The 10 hours can be organised across several supervised sessions as the centre arranges.

questions.q: Why is there no fixed page or size limit imposed on preparatory work?
options: Because preparatory work is not marked
So students can develop their response in a way appropriate to their intentions
Because only the final piece counts
Because it must fit a single sketchbook page
questions.explain: AQA allows preparatory work to take whatever form best supports the student's personal response.

questions.q: A student chooses the starting point 'Fragments' and immediately paints a large final canvas without research or experiments. Which requirement have they most clearly neglected?
options: The preparatory work developing and refining ideas
questions.explain: Producing a final piece without preparatory development neglects AO1 and AO2 shown through preparatory work.

questions.q: During the supervised time a student realises their final piece needs a new technique they have never tried. What is the best advice within the rules?
options: Take the work home to experiment there
Work within the supervised session and preparatory ideas already developed
Ask a teacher to complete the technique for them
questions.explain: The final piece must be produced under supervision, drawing on ideas already explored in preparatory work.

questions.q: Two students respond to the same starting point but produce very different outcomes in different media. According to AQA, is this acceptable?
options: No, all responses to a starting point must look similar
Yes, a starting point is intended to prompt personal and varied responses
No, students must agree on one medium
Yes, but only if they use the same artist reference
questions.explain: Starting points are deliberately open to encourage individual, personal interpretations.

questions.q: A student's preparatory work shows strong artist research and experiments but no drawings from observation. Which assessment objective is weakest?
questions.explain: Recording first-hand observations and insights is central to AO3, which is under-evidenced here.

questions.q: How does the supervised final piece relate to the preparatory work?
options: It is unrelated and started fresh with a new theme
It should resolve and bring together the ideas developed in the preparatory work
It replaces the need for any preparatory work
It must copy an artist's painting exactly
questions.explain: The final piece is the culmination that realises the intentions developed through preparatory work.

specSource: AQA GCSE Art and Design specification; Component 2: Externally Set Assignment
